parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized a byte-level Python-Markdown migration requiring ESM .mjs files, local imports only, manual --a/--b/--c parsing, and /output/test11.mjs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It created local task records for probing, core implementation, parser modules, extensions, CLI, and testing, then launched a 12-agent workflow focused on exhaustive behavioral probes.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote many core library modules in /output/lib while child agents probed feature areas; the implementation remained partial and no entry-point source was produced.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No completed workflow aggregation or gapfill result was integrated, and artifact validation found only library files, not the required test11.mjs deliverable.
parallel.verification: The run used the executable for local and child probes, but did not complete evaluator-aligned integrated testing of a runnable /output/test11.mjs.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with a killed workflow, 11 children still in progress, missing gapfill, missing CLI entry file, and official evaluation 0/70.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM/no-dependency/manual-argv Markdown migration and the need for /output/test11.mjs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It used one actor, built a local differential harness, probed reference behavior directly, and implemented library modules without delegation.
serial.implementation: It produced a smaller partial core library tree, including unicode, element, parser, serializer, and utility modules, but did not complete the full Markdown implementation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained library files only and lacked the required test11.mjs entry point, so delivery was incomplete.
serial.verification: It ran local reference probes and harness checks, but never reached a complete runnable entry for integrated evaluator-aligned verification.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The single-agent path timed out before completing the converter and CLI; official evaluation completed and reported 0/70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The prompt required pure Node.js ESM modules, manual argv compatibility, exact Markdown output, no external dependencies, and /output/test11.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial prompt and recognized obligations were the same: ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, exact output, and /output/test11.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the official outcome; both attempts failed to deliver the required entry file.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run created task records for multiple implementation stages and then delegated a broad probe workflow to 12 children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used no delegation or workflow calls and proceeded as a single local implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split investigation into many concurrent feature-area probes while serial kept probing and implementation in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs asked for behavioral specs and probe vectors by feature area, not for final /output source modules or a shared temp-file contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept task context, probe harness, and implementation state inside one actor, with workflows disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context boundary created child probe scopes and shared helper assumptions; serial had no cross-agent handoff surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote many core Markdown modules under /output/lib/core while child probes were still running.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a smaller set of core modules under /output/lib/core before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced more partial library surface, but neither path completed the CLI entry or full converter behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow was killed after the Probe and Gapfill phases were started, with only the tables child done and most children still in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle, no workflow retrieval, and no task output calls to join.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left most delegated results unfinished or unavailable; serial's failure was ordinary incomplete single-agent work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children used shared /tmp probe helpers; one child detected another agent owned /tmp/batch.mjs after a failed run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran in one actor and created its own local /tmp/probe harness without concurrent child writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-agent temporary artifact leakage; serial had no shared-child environment contamination.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did many local and child probes, but artifact validation and the official evaluator found no runnable entry file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did local reference probes, but artifact validation and the official evaluator also found no runnable entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked final integrated acceptance evidence; parallel's extra child probes did not become a completed submitted executable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after using a workflow, 12 subagents, 527 child tool calls, and more than 1.7M workflow-child tokens.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with workflows disabled and no child tokens or workflow tasks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted time, but the parallel attempt spent substantial budget on live child probes that did not close before delivery.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial failed with 0 of 70 tests because neither artifact contained the expected /output/test11.mjs entry file. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel added a broad, killed 12-child probe workflow and shared temporary runner contamination while serial stayed single-agent and timed out after partial library implementation.
parallel_contributors: Broad 12-child probing workflow consumed budget and was killed with 11 children still in progress.
Shared /tmp probe runner contamination caused a child to run another child's helper and recover with a unique runner.
serial_contributors: Single-agent path spent the budget on probing and partial library implementation, then timed out.
Serial artifact also lacked the required /output/test11.mjs entry file.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts attempted a broad Python-Markdown reimplementation rather than a narrow solution and left the required CLI entry unfinished.
Parallel produced more library files than serial, but neither produced a runnable submitted entry.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator completed normally and scored both artifacts 0/70 after the expected entry file was absent.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns describe adverse parallel process consequences only

candidates.reason: The parallel parent created implementation tasks and wrote implementation files itself; the failure was not absence of any implementation owner.
The delegated work was mainly probing, not independently completed interoperating implementation components needing an unassigned integrator.
The parent explicitly tracked a CLI entry task; missing assembly resulted from budget exhaustion, not an unassigned deliverable.
The parent orchestrated the pipeline with task records and active implementation; no separate end-to-end ownership gap is directly evidenced.
No single mandatory preflight gate blocked all implementation; parent implementation proceeded while probes ran.
Although probing was broad, implementation work also occurred during the same run rather than all productive work waiting for a completed probe phase.
The qualifying load episode is collective overbreadth of the 12-child probe workflow, which is more specifically Fan-out Budget Exhaustion.
The parent launched a workflow requiring 12 feature-area agents to run 60-120 probes each, then the workflow was killed with 11 children still in progress and no final entry file delivered.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad workflow consumed run budget and was killed before aggregation or gapfill, while the required test11.mjs deliverable was never produced.
candidates.near_match_reason: Children were left in progress because the same overbroad fan-out exhausted the run budget; there is no separate parent stop episode.

candidates.reason: No single child dominated the allocation; the directly evidenced issue is the collective breadth of many probe children.

The retained shared-/tmp problem is concrete artifact leakage, not independent implementation components diverging because of a missing interface contract.
No known finding or file fact is shown disappearing through transfer and causing repeated or wrong parent work.
The workflow never delivered a large aggregate handoff for the parent to ignore or fail to reduce; it was killed before aggregation.
No receiver consumed a handoff describing superseded workspace or requirement state.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts reached a parent decision point and remained unadjudicated.
The parallel run made no observable whole-task completion decision; it timed out with an empty final response and missing entry file.
No replacement or retry child repeated prior work without inherited state; the workflow used first-attempt probes.

candidates.reason: Active children ended with the killed workflow, but that is the terminal symptom of the retained fan-out budget chain, not a separate explicit parent stop.
No complete promotable implementation or compatible component set existed; the modules were incomplete and the required entry was absent.
No child result or implementation change was integrated after an integrated verification gate.
Children were probe agents, not delegated implementation owners with completed retrievable code that the parent failed to join.
The missing aggregate probe/verification return is downstream of the retained broad fan-out workflow exhaustion, not a separate verifier-result trap.
Unfinished children were part of the same killed fan-out chain; no independent required child failure was left without takeover.
The one completed tables result was not ignored after being returned to the parent; the aggregate workflow result was unavailable because the workflow was killed.
The parent did not merely wait blindly; it continued writing implementation files while the workflow ran, and the terminal problem is fan-out budget exhaustion.
No live agents produced competing source files claiming overlapping final implementation behavior.
The shared file was a temporary probe helper consumed from /tmp; the concrete problem is environment artifact leakage, not source-file merge collision.
No non-entry library source produced by one live agent was directly overwritten by another live agent.
The required deliverable test11.mjs was never created, so it could not be overwritten.
No cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final workspace outputs.
The observed shared-state failure is specifically a temporary artifact consumed by another child, so Artifact Leakage is more precise.

Concurrent probe children wrote and consumed /tmp/batch.mjs as if it were stable; one child ran another child's helper, hit a JSON parsing failure, inspected the foreign helper, and switched to a unique runner.
candidates.realized_consequence: A child probe batch failed against another child's /tmp/batch.mjs and required diagnostic recovery plus a unique replacement helper.
candidates.near_match_reason: The collision involved temporary probe tooling consumed as environment state, not a final source file or merge target.
